page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor featuring a dedicated allocation of 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The instance configuration includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). For high-throughput local operations, it incorporates 600 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps, with no GPUs attached and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark analysis reflects stable mid-tier compute capabilities alongside specific memory constraints. Multi-core performance is solid, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 19,599.25 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,050.0. However, single-core processing shows bottlenecks, registering 765.29 in stress-ng (placing in the bottom 10%). While cached small-block memory read bandwidth reaches 800.68 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths dip to 37.07 GB/sec and 22.42 GB/sec respectively (falling into the bottom 25%). The CPU features support for standard vector and cryptographic extensions like AES and SHA-NI, but it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions, which limits efficiency for larger matrix operations such as medium-tier LLM prompt processing.

The qualitative value of the c5ad.4xlarge lies in its pairing of AMD compute cores with integrated NVMe SSD local storage. This eliminates external network storage latency for scratch operations, caching, and temporary indexing. The instance is suitable for workloads requiring dedicated multi-threaded compute and fast local disk access, such as distributed CI/CD build environments, batch processing, video encoding, and intermediate data staging for ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance utilizing the AWS Nitro System and an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor clocked at 3.3 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it establishes a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio complemented by 600 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate mid-range multi-core CPU capacity, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,050.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 19,599.25, alongside average performance in compilation and web serving. Although uncached memory bandwidth and single-thread stress performance sit lower relative to peers, the local NVMe storage provides low-latency scratch space. This server is best suited for compute-heavy batch workloads, CI/CD build runners, caching layers, and ETL operations needing temporary storage.
